subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking scope & deliverable handoff
messages:
From: Kelsey Dawson <kelsey@neptunecloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Price <devon@neptunecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking scope & deliverable handoff

Marcus —

Thanks for picking this up. As we discussed in the call, Neptune needs a clear MAP deliverable set for the performance evaluation so we can sign the SOW and move to procurement. High-level asks from our side:

- Baseline and optimized results for key metrics: p50/p95 latency (end-to-end tokens), TTFT for chat flow, sustained throughput (tokens/s), and concurrency behavior at 50/200/500 active sessions.
- CSV exports with raw samples (latency by sample, concurrency stamp), and a slide deck with summarized charts and the executive TL;DR.
- A runbook / reproducible harness (docker-compose or script) that our SRE can run to validate results.
- Dashboard link (read-only) and an optional live demo during exec readout.

Target evaluation window: week of July 6 — we'd like the live exec readout the following week so procurement can close by July 20. Can you confirm scope, deliverables, and timeline? Also confirm whether the initial baseline will be run without prefix/KV caching and then with caching on as a separate run.

Thanks,
Kelsey
Director, Platform Eng — Neptune Cloud

[signature]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Dawson <kelsey@neptunecloud.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance benchmarking scope & deliverable handoff

Kelsey —

Appreciate the clear checklist. We can deliver exactly what you outlined. Attached is a short manifest that maps each MAP artifact to ownership and target delivery dates: [attachment: MAP_Benchmark_Manifest_v0.1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)].

Quick confirmation items so we align the runs:
- Model variant: "redwood/open-7b-v2-quant" (if you want a different variant, flag it).
- Hardware: dedicated skylake-v100 equivalent (we'll run the Dedicated pool unless you prefer hosted endpoints).
- Baseline runs: will execute first with caching disabled, then a second pass with KV/prefix cache enabled.
- Concurrency shaping: we propose stepped ramps at 50, 200, and 500 concurrent sessions (30-minute steady window each).

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- 06/26: Test harness & runbook sent to Neptune SRE (we'll attach run-harness-docker-stub.yml).
- 07/02–07/03: Dry runs/internal QA on our infra.
- 07/06–07/08: Customer-facing benchmark window (we'll stream telemetry to the dashboard link).
- 07/09: Deliver CSV exports + slide draft.
- 07/12–07/16: Exec readout slot availability — Marissa to confirm a specific date.

We'll include raw CSVs, a summarized slide deck, the runbook, and a link to an internal Grafana panel we can share read-only. If those dates work, we'll lock the calendar and start the dry-run.

Next steps: Soojin, can you confirm the exact telemetry fields we'll dump to CSV? Marissa, can you propose two 30-min exec readout slots?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead — Redwood Inference
[attachment: run-harness-docker-stub.yml]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kelsey Dawson <kelsey@neptunecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance benchmarking scope & deliverable handoff

Marcus / Kelsey —

Technical details from the bench team:

1) Telemetry / CSV fields we'll provide (raw + normalized):
   - timestamp_utc
   - request_id
   - model_variant
   - input_tokens
   - output_tokens
   - end_to_end_latency_ms
   - generation_latency_ms
   - ttft_ms (time-to-first-token)
   - server_cpu_pct / gpu_util_pct
   - concurrency_level
   - cache_hit (boolean)

2) Test harness notes:
   - We'll supply a docker-compose stub that spins a workload generator and collector. See attached runbook excerpt.
   - Seed prompt sets: 3 buckets (short, medium, long) with 200 samples each; we will randomize order to avoid synchronized bursts.
   - Quantization variants: float16 baseline, 4-bit quant run for cost/perf delta.

3) Measurement rules:
   - Each concurrency window will run for 30 minutes with the first 5 minutes discarded for warm-up.
   - Baseline run: caching disabled, standard batching (auto-batching tuned to latency SLO).
   - Cache-run: prefix/KV cache enabled; we'll report both aggregate and per-session deltas.

4) Artifacts to deliver:
   - latency_throughput_results.csv (raw rows + metadata header)
   - runbook (benchmark-runbook.md)
   - slide deck (exec-ready PDF)

If Neptune wants us to include p50/p95 confidence intervals and simple perf/regression charts, we will.

-- Soojin
Perf Engineer — Redwood Inference
[attachment: benchmark-runbook.md]

From: Kelsey Dawson <kelsey@neptunecloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Devon Price <devon@neptunecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance benchmarking scope & deliverable handoff

Thanks — this looks good. A couple of clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

- We absolutely want the baseline (no cache) first, then cache-on. Please also include a hybrid run where cache hit rate is realistic (we can provide a sample traffic trace).
- For the exec one-pager: can you include a single slide that lists acceptance criteria (e.g., p95 < 300 ms for text gen; TTFT < 700 ms for chat) and the delta between baseline/optimized? That will help procurement sign-off.

If you can get the runbook + dashboard link by Monday (06/29), we'll confirm the July 6 window.

Kelsey

I've attached an exec brief template that we'll populate with the TL;DR, acceptance criteria, and top-line charts. Also noting: procurement requested an SOW signature by July 20 — if the results meet the acceptance criteria we can attach the SOW and ask Neptune to sign after the exec readout.

Marissa Cole

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final artifacts: CSVs, deck, runbook + dashboard link (for July 6–8 window)

Kelsey —

We completed the internal dry-runs and packaged the MAP artifacts for the customer-facing window. Attached and links below:

Attachments included in this email:
- latency_throughput_results.csv (raw telemetry + metadata header)
- MAP_Benchmark_Manifest_v0.1.pdf (artifact checklist, owners, delivery dates)
- benchmark-runbook.md (how to replay the runs; includes docker stub)
- exec-brief-deck_v1.pdf (9 slides, TL;DR + charts + acceptance criteria)

Related links (read-only):
- Performance dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/boards/NEPTUNE-789?view=perf-summary
- Shared drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSharedDriveLink

Top-line acceptance criteria we propose for the exec: (these will be in the one-pager slide)
- p95 end-to-end latency <= 250 ms for text-gen workload (baseline + cache runs reported separately).
- TTFT <= 600 ms on chat priming flows.
- Sustained throughput >= 12k tokens/s per 8xA100 equivalent (numbers normalized in CSV).

Next steps:
1) Neptune SRE to validate runbook on their side (we've included docker-compose stub).
2) Live benchmark window 07/06–07/08 (we'll stream telemetry to the dashboard link).
3) Deliver CSV + exec deck by 07/09 for final slide updates.
4) Exec readout 07/08 at 11:00 AM PT (Marissa to finalize).

If the metrics meet the acceptance criteria, we'll proceed to finalize the SOW and DocuSign flow. Please confirm and I'll lock the calendar invites.

Thanks — looking forward to the readout.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead — Redwood Inference
